## Model

For a sample-by-feature matrix $X=(x_{ij})$, MPCurve represents a latent
ordering by $K$ grid positions. In the single-ordering model, sample $i$ has
an unobserved position $C_i$, and feature $j$ has a trajectory
$U_j=(u_{j1},\ldots,u_{jK})$. Conditional on $C_i=k$, the Gaussian observation
model centers $x_{ij}$ at $u_{jk}$. A Gaussian Markov random-field prior on
$U_j$ encourages smooth changes across adjacent grid positions. The model can
estimate feature-specific noise variances or use supplied measurement standard
deviations.

## Variational inference

MPCurver 0.3.0 fits MPCurve using coordinate-ascent variational inference
(CAVI). It alternates updates of sample
position probabilities, posterior distributions for the feature trajectories,
and model parameters. The trajectory posterior records both a mean and
uncertainty. The evidence lower bound (ELBO) tracks progress for the
single-ordering fit.

The [MPCurver getting-started
article](https://aguerozz.github.io/MPCurver/articles/mpcurve_intro.html) gives
the equations, CAVI updates, and an executable spiral example.

## Several orderings

When different feature groups may describe different sample patterns, set
`intrinsic_dim = M` to fit a specified number $M$ of orderings. Each feature
has a latent assignment $Z_j$ to an ordering. The structural variational
family includes $q(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j)$, so a candidate trajectory is
conditional on the feature's ordering assignment. CAVI estimates the sample
positions, conditional trajectories, and feature-assignment probabilities
together.

An assignment probability near one supports a particular ordering for a
feature; a diffuse row indicates uncertainty. The ordering labels and
directions are arbitrary, so interpretation uses observed annotations and
trajectory shapes.

The number of orderings $M$ is specified before fitting. The [feature-partitioning
article](https://aguerozz.github.io/MPCurver/articles/partition.html) develops
the structural model and its updates in detail.

The [simulation pages](simulation_m1.html) compare fitted orderings with known
